title: AI Asset Management in the AI Security Admin Portal: what it inventories, signing in, first-time configuration order, table behavior

prose.text: {{infra-discovery-scope}} {{resource-inventory}} {{public-ai-usage}} Which AI platforms are supported is open {{gap:ai-platform-support}}.

checks.do: For a sign-in problem, whether the user has an active Authentication Service user account and the AI Security entitlement enabled for it.
Table settings that seem lost after a different browser or a cleared cache.

signin-prereqs.statement: Signing in to the AI Security Admin Portal requires an active Authentication Service user account and the AI Security entitlement enabled for that user account.

quotes: An active Authentication Service user account (username and password).
AI Security entitlement enabled for your user account to access the Zscaler AI Security Admin Portal.

signin-routes.statement: The AI Security Admin Portal can be reached three ways: directly at ai-console.zscaler.com, from the Authentication Service Portal at <tenant>.zslogin.net (subdomain and domain may vary by tenant), or from the Experience Center at console.zscaler.com.

quotes: Open the AI Security Admin Portal (URL: https://ai-console.zscaler.com/dashboard).
Open the Authentication Service Portal (URL: https://<tenant>.zslogin.net/portal).
The subdomain and domain may vary by tenant.
Log in to the Experience Center (URL: https://console.zscaler.com).

infra-discovery-scope.statement: AI infrastructure discovery inventories models, MCP servers, agents and AI apps, with dashboard metrics for risk-level, type, environment and cloud distribution and drill-down from widgets to inventory lists.

quotes: Asset discovery and inventory of key AI infrastructure components, including, models, MCP servers, agents, and AI apps.
High-level metrics and distributions such as, risk-level distribution, type-based distribution (e.g., model types), environment and cloud distribution.
Interactive drill-down from dashboard widgets into detailed inventory lists for each asset type.

resource-inventory.statement: AI Security gives an inventory-style view of five supporting resource types: workloads, datastores, identities, guardrails and AI software libraries; libraries appear as data becomes available.

quotes: Workloads: Compute and services that host or run AI-related components.
Datastores: Storage locations used by AI workloads and pipelines.
Identities: Users and service identities that access AI assets and resources.
Guardrails: Controls and configurations that help enforce safe and compliant AI usage.
AI software libraries: Libraries detected in the environment (appear as data becomes available).

public-ai-usage.statement: Public AI visibility covers usage analytics (traffic volume, user counts, top-used apps, department-wise usage), category-based views by AI app type, and MCP traffic visibility.

quotes: Usage analytics includes overall traffic volume, user counts, top-used apps, and department-wise usage.
Category-based views to understand usage by AI app type (e.g., GenAI, Desktop AI, Embedded AI).
MCP traffic visibility to help monitor AI-related traffic patterns.

config-steps.statement: The configuration guide lists nine steps in order: set up the account, DLP engines and sensitive data, onboard cloud accounts, scan settings, users, business units, AI posture policies, issue rules, and external integrations and notifications.

quotes: Step 1: Set up Your Account
Step 2: Set up the DLP Engines and Define Sensitive Data
Step 3: Onboard Cloud Accounts
Step 4: Configure Scan Settings
Step 5: Configure Users
Step 6: Configure Business Units
Step 7: Configure the AI Posture Policies
Step 8: Configure Issue Rules
Step 9: Configure External Integrations and Notifications

dlp-synced.statement: AI Security classifies data types with predefined DLP engines and dictionaries synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA).

quotes: AI Security uses predefined DLP engines and dictionaries that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA) to classify data types.

registration-email.statement: Once the organization is provisioned for AI Security, a registration email is sent to complete account setup.

quotes: After your organization is provisioned for AI Security, you receive an email to complete the registration.

tables-settings-storage.statement: Table setting changes in the AI Security Admin Portal are kept in the browser local storage and are lost if the cache is cleared or a different browser is used; not all settings are available for all tables.

quotes: Every time you make a change, the settings are stored in your browser's local storage so that your changes are preserved the next time you log on.
If you clear your cache or use a different browser, your settings are lost.
Not all settings are available for all tables.

tables-columns-search.statement: For some tables at least one column must stay visible; resetting columns to default does not affect sort order; table search shows matching rows even when the term is in a hidden column.

quotes: For some tables, you must have at least one column visible at all times.
Resetting columns to default settings does not affect sort order.
The search results display the applicable rows even if the term is in a hidden column.

ai-platform-support.title: Which AI platforms AI Security supports
ai-platform-support.detail: Understanding AI Security names AWS Bedrock, Azure Foundry, Hugging Face and Ollama only as examples; no support matrix is given.
